Add only two distinct complete visual configurations, not more melancholy synonyms.

sources.title: Getty: Richard Learoyd: In the Studio
sources.supports: Getty discusses contemplative affect and viewer intimacy in photographs of figures, portraits and still lifes; mood is not limited to facial expression. This supports an interpretive role, not any universal visual formula.

sources.title: Getty: The Window in the History of Photography
sources.supports: Getty describes framing and figure-window relations as tools for enigmatic or suspenseful readings, including unresolved anticipation. The same visible motif has formal, social and metaphorical uses.

sources.title: The Met: Richard Avedon: Portraits
sources.supports: The catalogue distinguishes the melancholy character collaboratively made in a portrait from disclosure of the sitter as a real person. This directly supports separating photographic interpretation from verified private emotion.

baseline.top8_assessment: Top results emphasize station staff, object absence, travel access barriers, contempt facial motion and pause rather than coherent mood. This is an exposure measurement, not a corpus absence proof.

inspection.method: Read hash-checked BodyReader records across all 18,250 canonical CIDs (including 70 diagnostic records); decode every record through installed photo_canonical_source.native, rather than comparing raw V3/V4. Inspect full native fields, not tags as an eligibility filter. Review 268 atmosphere-effect records plus cross-dimensional affect/narrative matches. Compare complete working V3 content, conditions and effects for four central existing mood/location CIDs; observed meanings match the decoded installed source.
inspection.limitation: Semantic search terms were used to organize full-source review, not to prefilter retrieval population or certify exhaustive natural-language equivalence. Native approval remains unclaimed.

confusion_boundaries: Scene mood is an optional affective reading, not proof of a sitter’s private emotion, mental health, memory, relationship history or an actual departure.
Sparse architecture and being unaccompanied can be calm or practical; emptiness alone does not prove loneliness, poverty, abandonment or danger.
Fog, dust, humidity and colored light may be independent physical or stylistic features; they are not required mood ingredients.
A station, an action pause or a face expression may carry a reading but does not substitute for the scene-level affect role.
Nostalgia does not require retro capture, and vintage texture does not establish genuine remembered events.
Concrete arrangements introduce actual pose/object/composition/lighting changes; candidates declare all affected dimensions and must pass their independent locks.
recommendations: Retain existing generic affect labels; do not add aliases or rewrite the original query to improve this known test.
Integrate at most the two authored relational configurations if independent semantic review accepts their effects; they are optional scene choices, not implicit mood defaults.

Run the identical original query after a full qualified rebuild, preserving before/after ranks of existing melancholy CIDs as well as new candidates. A new candidate entering top8 is insufficient if its full scene violates frozen properties.
Also test diverse out-of-probe mood intents and inspect returned complete sources. Keep discovery and native qualification separate.
